Chantani Museum is in the village of the same name on the northern side of the Uyuni Salt Flat, between Tahua and Coquesa. This small local museum is dedicated to the region's natural and cultural heritage. A visit adds another dimension to a trip across the salt flat and an introduction to the villages at the foot of Tunupa.

Here you can learn about everyday life on the Altiplano and see objects used by local residents. On the tour itinerary, the museum stop is combined with Colchani, Incahuasi Island and lunch on the salt flat. The visiting time depends on the route of the particular trip.

Trails through Chapada dos Guimarães National Park wind among sandstone cliffs and canyons. Water and wind have shaped the distinctive landforms, while nature trails connect areas of vegetation and waterfalls.

Excursion itineraries include the White Bride waterfall. A visit to the park highlights its combination of waterways, rocky landscapes and savanna, and can be paired with a trip through the Northern Pantanal.

Chapada dos Guimarães is visited on trips from the Cuiabá area. Itineraries include an introduction to the historic center and the Geodesic Marker of South America.

The town stop complements excursions to nearby cliffs, canyons and waterfalls. The town and the national park of the same name are separate places: the town offers an insight into local life, while the park focuses on natural landscapes.

## Panorama of the Plateau

Mirante do Centro Geodésico is a viewpoint stop near Chapada dos Guimarães. The tour itinerary visits it after exploring the town's historic center and before checking in at Park Eco Lodge.

The viewpoint offers sweeping vistas of the surrounding plains. After a boat trip in Bom Jardim, the contrast between landscapes is particularly striking here: clear rivers give way to the wide-open spaces and cliffs of the plateau.

On the itinerary and in local tourist materials, the viewpoint is known as the “Geodesic Center of South America.” Above all, the trip here is an opportunity to admire the surrounding landscape from above.

In Chapultepec, the bustle of Mexico City gradually gives way to footsteps along a shaded path. Tree canopies meet overhead, lakes appear between the trees, and a walk offers a chance to catch your breath after the busy streets. This large urban park has long been linked to the capital's history: important freshwater springs were located here even in pre-Hispanic times.

Chapultepec Castle stands in the park's first section. A visit introduces you to Mexico's history and offers views of the city from the hill. Nearby are a botanical garden and traces of old waterworks. The National Museum of Anthropology is on the park's edge, so you can easily spend a day combining a walk and a museum visit at your own pace.

Chapultepec is far larger than any single walking route. There are lakes in the second section, while different parts of the park have their own cultural spaces. Choose a few places that especially interest you and leave time for an unhurried stroll. Sit by the water, look at the trees and experience how green spaces thrive in this vast city.
